disease.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV)
disease.severity_index: Can cause 30–90% yield loss if uncontrolled

favorable_weather_conditions.vector_activity: Whitefly population increases during warm, humid periods

environmental_factors.temperature_humidity: Prefers warm, humid climates with limited rainfall
environmental_factors.soil_conditions: More severe in rainfed cotton areas with dense plantings

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: Coastal districts face higher disease prevalence due to humid conditions
region_specific_information.Telangana: Rainfed cotton areas like Warangal and Karimnagar are more affected

early_stage: Thickened and dark green veins on leaves
advanced_stage: No flowering or fruiting, leading to heavy yield loss

resistant_varieties: Bt Cotton (Bollgard II) with tolerance to CLCuV
crop_rotation: Destroy infected cotton plants immediately after harvest
soil_seed_treatment: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid @ 5 g/kg seed to reduce early-stage vector attack

cultural_practices: Early sowing in June-July reduces whitefly infestation risks
Use of yellow sticky traps (5 per acre) to monitor vector activity
Remove weeds and alternate hosts (okra, hibiscus) to limit virus spread
biological_control: Releasing Chrysoperla carnea (Green Lacewing) to feed on whiteflies
Neem oil spray @ 5 ml/L water as a repellent
